acceptor_preferences.description: The ranked preference lists of the accepting partition (e.g., hospitals or schools) in stable matching.

accumulate_supersets_instead.description: A flag for SOS DP indicating whether to sum over supersets instead of subsets.

add_element_fn.description: A delegate function used in Mo's algorithm to add an element's contribution to the current window state.

add_fn.description: A function to process the addition of an element or state update.

addend_a.description: The first integer operand in a bitwise addition operation.

addend_b.description: The second integer operand in a bitwise addition operation.

aggregation_function.description: A function that combines multiple values into a single summary value (e.g., sum, min, max).

aggregation_operator.description: The associative binary operator used to merge values along a path or within a range.

allow_diagonal_moves.description: A flag indicating if 8-directional movement is permitted instead of just 4-directional on a grid.

allow_duplicates.description: Specifies whether a data structure or generator should accept or yield identical elements.

allow_element_reuse.description: A backtracking constraint flag that dictates if the same candidate can be chosen multiple times.

allow_empty_subarray.description: If true, the maximum sum subarray is allowed to be empty (returning 0) if all elements are negative.

allow_empty_submatrix.description: If true, the maximum sum submatrix is allowed to be 0 by selecting no cells.

allow_shared_endpoints.description: Dictates if intervals [a,b] and [b,c] are considered overlapping (false) or disjoint (true).

allowed_column_shifts.description: The permissible horizontal movements (e.g., [-1, 0, 1]) when dropping to the next row in grid DP.

allowed_directions.description: The valid movement vectors (e.g., Right and Down) allowed during grid traversal.

allowed_operators.description: The set of mathematical operators (e.g., '+', '-', '*') that can be inserted in an expression evaluator.

allowed_step_sizes.description: The exact number of steps a user can take at once (e.g., [1, 2]) in climbing stairs problems.

alphabet_size.description: The total number of distinct characters or symbols in the sequence's character set.

array_a.description: The first input array, usually representing coefficients or values for convolution/multiplication.

array_b.description: The second input array, usually representing coefficients or values for convolution/multiplication.

associated_metadata.description: Optional arbitrary data stored alongside a key or word at a terminal node in a Trie.

associativity_map.description: A mapping defining whether operators are left-associative or right-associative.

augmented_or_square_matrix.description: A 2D array representing a system of linear equations, optionally combined with the right-hand side vector.

balloon_values.description: The numeric sequence representing the multipliers of balloons to be optimally burst.

bar_width.description: The horizontal width of each bar in a histogram (defaults to 1).

base_a.description: The base integer operand being raised to a power in modular exponentiation or Pollard's p-1.

base_case_cutoff_size.description: The threshold below which a divide-and-conquer algorithm falls back to a naive/iterative approach.

base_cases.description: The predefined starting values for the lowest states in a Dynamic Programming tabulation.

base_element.description: The element to be multiplied by itself repeatedly in exponentiation algorithms.

base_g.description: The generator or base element in discrete logarithm algorithms.

base_interval_values.description: Initial base values for intervals of length 1 in interval DP algorithms.

base_multiplier.description: The base/radix value used to shift previous hash values in a rolling hash function.

binary_constraint_matrix.description: A 2D array of 0s and 1s representing subsets and universe elements in the exact cover problem.

binary_keys_list.description: A list of binary representations used to construct a bit-index branching structure like a Patricia Trie.

binary_operator.description: A function that takes two arguments and combines them into a single result (e.g., sum, xor).

bit_count_n.description: The total number of bits or boolean variables defining the size of the subset state space.

bit_count_or_index_n.description: The bit length of the Gray code sequence to generate, or the specific index to compute.

bit_sequence_or_integer.description: The binary data structure whose set bits (1s) are to be counted.

bit_width.description: The exact number of bits representing the integer, used to bound shifts and reversals.

bitmask_m.description: An integer whose set bits represent the active elements of a specific subset.

bitwise_operation_type.description: Specifies whether the Walsh-Hadamard transform should perform XOR, AND, or OR convolution.

block_size.description: The chunk size to divide an array or tree into for square-root decomposition or jumping.

blocked_cells_mask.description: A bitmask identifying which cells in the current profile column/row are impassable.

board_columns.description: The total number of vertical columns on a given 2D grid/board.

board_grid.description: The 2D state of the game board (e.g., Sudoku) containing given values and empty cells.

board_rows.description: The total number of horizontal rows on a given 2D grid/board.

board_size_n.description: The dimension of an N x N square grid (e.g., for the N-Queens problem).

boolean_expression.description: A sequence of alternating boolean values ('T', 'F') and operators ('&', '|', '^').

bound_value_x.description: The limit used in range operations like chmin (a_i = min(a_i, X)) or chmax.

boundary_is_inside.description: Defines whether points lying exactly on a polygon's boundary are treated as strictly inside.

boundary_multiplier_value.description: The implicit value of the out-of-bounds elements (usually 1 in Burst Balloons).

bounding_box.description: The 2D coordinate limits defining the outer perimeter for Voronoi cells or intersections.

bounding_box_limits.description: The [min_x, max_x, min_y, max_y] rectangle acting as the initial infinite plane limits.

bounding_function.description: A heuristic function that calculates the optimistic upper/lower bound of a partial state to prune branches.

box_types_array.description: An array where each tuple contains [number_of_boxes, units_per_box].

bracket_pairs_map.description: A mapping of closing brackets to their corresponding opening brackets (e.g., ')' -> '(').

buffer_capacity.description: The maximum number of items or pages the memory structure can hold.

bwt_string.description: The transformed string generated by the Burrows-Wheeler Transform, usually containing clustered characters.

c1_coefficient.description: The linear coefficient used in the quadratic probing hash formula.

c2_coefficient.description: The quadratic coefficient used in the quadratic probing hash formula.

cache_capacity.description: The maximum number of distinct keys the cache is allowed to store.

cache_table.description: An optional external memory store passed into a memoization function to persist state.

candidate_subtree_root.description: The root of the smaller tree being checked to see if it exists entirely within the main tree.

candidate_vertices_p.description: The set of vertices that can potentially be added to the current clique.

candidates_array.description: The pool of available numeric values that can be combined to reach a target sum.

capacity_k.description: The fixed maximum size limit for a circular queue or bounded structure.

character_alphabet_size.description: The number of distinct characters allowed (e.g., 26 for English letters) used to size frequency arrays.

character_board.description: A 2D grid of letters used in word search or Boggle solvers.

checkpoint_timestamp.description: A historical marker used to rollback a DSU or persistent data structure to a specific previous state.

choose_count_k.description: The exact number of items to select in combination generation algorithms.

circular_house_values.description: An array of house loot values where the first and last elements are considered adjacent.

close_delimiter.description: The symbol representing the end of an encoded or nested sequence.

closed_tour_required.description: A flag indicating if the knight must end exactly one move away from its starting position.

cluster_merge_fn.description: A delegate that dictates how two tree clusters are merged into a single parent cluster in Top Trees.

coefficients_array.description: An array representing the coefficients of a polynomial, ordered by degree.

coefficient_matrix.description: The matrix of multipliers representing the left-hand side of a system of linear equations.

coin_denominations.description: The set of available coin values used to make change.

color_count_k.description: The number of distinct colors available for painting fences or vertices.

column_count_n.description: The total number of columns representing the width of a grid.

combination_function.description: The logic to merge two partial states from divided halves in Meet-in-the-Middle.

combine_parent_fn.description: A function that computes a node's full state by incorporating the aggregated value of its parent.

comparator.description: A lambda function defining the relative sorting order or priority comparison of two elements.

comparable_characters.description: Implies the string characters possess a defined lexicographical order.

complete_future_access_sequence.description: Indicates that the algorithm requires full a priori knowledge of all future memory accesses.

composite_integer_n.description: A non-prime integer that is the target of a factorization algorithm.

condition_predicate.description: A boolean function used by Two-Pointer techniques to decide whether to advance the left or right pointer.

connectivity_directions.description: Defines whether cells share a region via edge-sharing (4-way) or corner-sharing (8-way).

connectivity_queries_list.description: A list of queries asking if node U is connected to node V at specific points in time.

constraint_matrix_a.description: The matrix representing the linear inequalities bounding the feasible region in the Simplex algorithm.

convex_polygon_a.description: The ordered vertices of the first convex polygon used in a Minkowski sum.

convex_polygon_b.description: The ordered vertices of the second convex polygon used in a Minkowski sum.

convex_polygon_vertices.description: The sequence of points defining the perimeter of a strictly convex shape.

cooldown_days.description: The mandatory waiting period (in days/steps) after a stock sale before a new purchase can occur.

coprime_base_and_modulus.description: Ensures the base and the modulus share no common factors other than 1, a requirement for discrete logs.

coprime_to_modulus.description: Ensures the integer shares no common factors with the modulus, ensuring a unique multiplicative inverse.

cost_function.description: The mathematical formula defining the cost of transitioning between DP states.

cost_grid.description: A 2D array where each cell represents the cost or penalty of stepping onto it.

cost_matrix.description: A 2D array representing the cost of assigning a specific resource (e.g., color, worker) to a target.

count_delta.description: The frequency or weight to add to the element in a Count-Min Sketch.

count_edges_instead_of_nodes.description: If true, tree height/diameter is measured by the number of edges. If false, by the number of vertices.

count_only_mode.description: If true, the backtracking algorithm returns the total number of solutions without storing them.

count_or_longest_mode.description: Specifies whether the algorithm should return the total number of valid subarrays or the length of the longest.

cookie_sizes_array.description: An array representing the available sizes of cookies to be distributed.

current_bitmask.description: The binary representation of the current active state or subset.

current_clique_r.description: The subset of vertices currently forming a completely connected clique in Bron-Kerbosch.

cut_cost.description: An optional flat penalty subtracted every time the rod is partitioned.

cyclic_group_elements.description: Assumes the inputs belong to a mathematical cyclic group for discrete logarithm computation.

de_bruijn_constant.description: A specific magic number used for O(1) bit scanning via multiplication and shifting.

default_empty_token.description: The character or token returned when a stream has no non-repeating characters available.

default_empty_value.description: The value returned by a sliding window query when no valid element meets the criteria.

default_not_found_value.description: The placeholder value (often -1) inserted into the result array when no greater/smaller element exists.

degeneracy_ordering_outer_loop.description: An optimization to iterate vertices by degeneracy order to bound the worst-case runtime.

delete_cost.description: The relative penalty weight assigned to deleting a character in edit distance.

deletion_cost.description: The cost of skipping an element from the sequence in sequence alignment algorithms.

delimiter.description: The token used to separate serialized node values in a string representation.

delimiter_char.description: A dummy character (e.g., '#') inserted between all sequence characters to unify odd/even palindrome logic.

denominator.description: The lower half of the fraction being decomposed in Egyptian fractions.

depth_d.description: The number of independent hash functions (rows) used in a Count-Min Sketch.

destination_cell.description: The target row/column coordinate in a maze solving or grid pathfinding problem.

deterministic_witness_bases.description: A specific, precomputed set of prime bases that guarantees deterministic primality testing for bounds like 2^64.

digit_string.description: A sequence of numeric characters representing a large number or encoded sequence.

dimensions_array.description: An array where element i and i+1 represent the rows and columns of matrix i.

direction.description: Specifies the movement vector, usually 'left' or 'right', for array or list rotations.

distance_metric.description: The mathematical formula (e.g., Euclidean, Manhattan) used to measure the distance between two points.

dividend.description: The number being divided in a bitwise division algorithm.

divisor.description: The number by which the dividend is divided.

domain_high.description: The maximum possible coordinate or independent variable in the query space.

domain_low.description: The minimum possible coordinate or independent variable in the query space.

edge_events_list.description: A timeline of edge insertions and deletions defining the dynamic state of a graph.

egg_count_k.description: The total number of available test items (eggs) that can break.

element.description: The item or value being queried, inserted, or tracked within a probabilistic structure.

element_to_enqueue.description: The value entering the back of a Queue structure.

element_to_insert.description: The value being added to a data structure like a Heap or Bloom Filter.

element_to_push.description: The value entering the top of a Stack structure.

element_u.description: The primary element or set identifier involved in a Disjoint Set operation.

element_v.description: The secondary element or set identifier involved in a Disjoint Set operation.

element_value.description: The payload associated with an insertion or manipulation operation.

empty_cell_marker.description: The specific value (often 0 or '.') that denotes a blank, unfilled cell in a grid puzzle.

encoded_string.description: The compressed or run-length nested string that needs to be expanded.

encoding_arity_d.description: The branching factor of the Huffman tree, defining a base-d prefix code instead of binary.

end_index.description: The 0-based inclusive ending bound for an operation on a linear sequence.

end_node.description: An optional stopping boundary for iterative list operations that don't traverse to null.

entry_root_vertex.description: The designated starting node defining the control flow dominance hierarchy.

entry_vertex.description: The arbitrary starting node used to begin centroid identification.

eof_sentinel_char.description: A unique, lexicographically smallest symbol (e.g., '$') appended to indicate the end of a BWT string.

epsilon_tolerance.description: The accepted mathematical deviation when testing floating point numbers for equality.

events_and_queries_list.description: A combined array of time-stamped updates and queries sorted by coordinate for CDQ.

excluded_vertices_x.description: Vertices that have already been explored and cannot form a new maximal clique in Bron-Kerbosch.

exponent_b.description: The target power to which a base is raised.

exponent_high_bound.description: The upper limit of the search space for Pollard's Kangaroo discrete logarithm.

exponent_low_bound.description: The lower limit of the search space for Pollard's Kangaroo discrete logarithm.

exponent_n.description: The target power to which a base element or matrix is raised.

fast_step_size.description: The number of nodes the fast pointer traverses per iteration (usually 2).

find_all_solutions.description: If true, the backtracking algorithm searches the entire state space to yield every valid answer.

find_all_subsets.description: If true, subset algorithms yield every valid combination instead of just true/false.

find_maximum.description: If true, tree extrema searches or ternary searches hunt for the largest value rather than the smallest.

floor_count_n.description: The total number of levels/floors to test in the egg dropping problem.

fractional_lp_solution.description: The continuous probability values (between 0 and 1) representing relaxed linear programming decisions.

gap_heuristic.description: An optimization for Push-Relabel that quickly disconnects nodes when a height gap is detected.

gap_sequence.description: The diminishing intervals defining which elements are compared and swapped during Shell Sort.

gas_available_array.description: An array representing the fuel provided at each station along a circular route.

geometric_events.description: A sorted collection of geometry changes (starts, ends, intersections) driving a sweep-line.

global_relabeling_heuristic.description: An optimization that periodically recalculates exact distances to the sink via reverse BFS in Push-Relabel.

greed_factors_array.description: The minimum cookie size required to satisfy each child.

grid.description: The primary 2D array representation of the environment or DP states.

grid_columns.description: The total width of the grid used for state compression bounds.

grid_rows.description: The total height of the grid used for state compression bounds.

group_size.description: The chunk length used to recursively divide elements in Median of Medians (typically 5).

group_size_k.description: The exact number of nodes inside each batch that undergoes reversal.

handle_duplicates.description: A flag dictating whether the subset generator should skip identical duplicate states.

hash_family.description: A collection of distinct hashing algorithms used to populate LSH bands or signatures.

hash_function.description: A specific custom logic used to map arbitrary keys to numeric bucket indices.

hash_function_seed.description: A randomly initialized constant used to prevent deterministic collisions during tree isomorphism hashing.

hash_functions_list.description: A set of independent hash functions used simultaneously to set bits in a Bloom Filter.

head_node.description: The primary reference pointer indicating the first element of a Linked List.

head_node_a.description: The starting pointer of the first Linked List operand.

head_node_b.description: The starting pointer of the second Linked List operand.

head_or_start_node.description: The entry point for pointer tracking, applicable to both linked lists and functional graphs.

heap_size.description: The virtual bound of the array currently representing the active heap structure.

heuristic_function.description: An optimistic distance estimator used to guide A* Search.

high_bound.description: The upper limit of the search space for binary or ternary optimization.

high_bound_r.description: The maximum inclusive integer forming the ceiling of a Segmented Sieve.

high_index.description: The upper boundary index governing the rightmost limit of a recursive split or search.

high_key.description: The inclusive upper limit value for an orthogonal or tree range query.

high_value.description: The largest pivot category used in Dutch National Flag ternary partitioning.

house_values.description: The amount of loot stored at each sequential position along a street.

identity_element.description: The neutral value that, when combined with any element using the binary operator, returns the element (e.g., 0 for sum, infinity for min).

include_collinear_boundary_points.description: Determines whether points lying exactly flat on the convex hull edge are kept or discarded.

include_endpoints.description: If true, intersections happening exactly at the start or end of a segment are counted as valid.

include_null_nodes_between_endpoints.description: Dictates whether empty spaces in a tree level are counted toward the total width calculation.

include_zero_mask.description: If true, the empty set (000...0) is returned as a valid submask during iteration.

incoming_character.description: A single element added to the streaming queue for non-repeating analysis.

index_n.description: The discrete time step or term sequence number to evaluate.

index_or_node_to_delete.description: The specific internal location or reference of the element to be removed from a Heap.

infix_expression.description: A mathematical string formatted with operators between operands (e.g., A + B).

initial_bound.description: The first step size used before doubling begins in Exponential Search.

initial_capacity.description: The predefined starting size of the underlying buckets array to prevent early resizing.

initial_delta_threshold.description: The starting power-of-two magnitude used for augmenting only large-capacity paths first.

initial_hull_size_guess.description: The starting estimate (m) for the final hull size in Chan's algorithm, usually squared repeatedly.

initial_incumbent_bound.description: A starting best-known value passed to Branch and Bound to immediately enable pruning.

initial_mask.description: The starting bitset representing pre-occupied or pre-selected states before DP begins.

initial_state_vector.description: The 1D column vector representing the base case or state at time t=0 for matrix exponentiation.

initial_terms.description: The predefined starting values (f(0)...f(k-1)) of a linear recurrence.

initial_value_x0.description: The deterministic or random seed initiating the tortoise and hare sequence in Pollard's Rho.

input_string.description: The raw sequence of characters provided to text algorithms or data compression encoders.

insert_cost.description: The relative penalty weight assigned to inserting a new character in edit distance.

insertion_cost.description: The cost of creating a gap element in the sequence during alignment.

integer_a.description: The first primary numeric operand in a number-theoretic or Euclidean algorithm.

integer_b.description: The second primary numeric operand in a number-theoretic or Euclidean algorithm.

integer_matrix.description: A grid containing strictly whole numbers, intended for fraction-free row reduction.

integer_n.description: A generalized generic whole number passed for bitwise manipulation or primality testing.

intervals_list.description: A collection of [start, end] pairs representing spans of time or space.

invert_transform_flag.description: If true, the mathematical transform runs in reverse (e.g., iFFT) to convert from point-value back to coefficients.

is_circular.description: Dictates whether searches over boundaries loop back to the beginning modulo the array size.

item_sizes.description: The sequence of weights or dimensions of items that need to be grouped into bins.

iteration_budget_k.description: A hard stop threshold limiting the maximum number of probabilistic trials run by Monte Carlo.

iteration_count_k.description: The number of independent randomized tests executed to bound the error margin of a primality check.

jobs_list.description: A collection of items defining [deadline, profit] for task scheduling.

jump_function.description: A pseudorandom mapping used to dictate the distance of the next 'hop' in Pollard's Kangaroo.

k_choose.description: The subset size parameter 'k' in the binomial coefficient C(n, k).

k_count.description: The total number of most frequent items to retrieve.

k_digits_to_remove.description: The exact number of characters to drop from a sequence to optimize the remaining result.

k_length.description: An optional constraint limiting the output permutation generation to a fixed partial size.

k_or_target_value.description: The element to query frequency for, or the rank 'k' when searching a Wavelet Tree.

k_rank.description: The 1-based order statistic representing the target position in sorted order.

k_step.description: The exact number of edges to traverse along a calculated tree path.

k_steps.description: The number of parent pointers to jump upwards in a binary lifting query.

key.description: The unique identifier serving as the primary index in a Hash Table or cache.

key_extractor.description: A lambda mapped over complex objects to isolate the numeric value used for Counting Sort.

key_string.description: A specialized string identifier used in O(1) tracking structures.

key_to_delete.description: The identifier of the node to be located and excised from the BST.

key_to_insert.description: The sorting identifier for a new node being introduced to the BST.

key_u.description: The first search value when isolating an LCA in a binary search tree.

key_v.description: The second search value when isolating an LCA in a binary search tree.

keys_array.description: The ordered sequence of actual search terms associated with an Optimal BST.

keys_list.description: The collection of raw inputs compiled together to form a compressed Radix Trie.

key_vertices_subset.description: A selected minority of tree nodes around which a compressed Virtual Tree is constructed.

knapsack_capacity.description: The strict maximum weight constraint defining the bounds of the optimization problem.

layer_count_k.description: The maximum number of splits, partitions, or sequential stages permitted in divide-and-conquer DP.

leaf_cutoff_dimension.description: The submatrix size at which Strassen's algorithm aborts recursion and applies standard matrix multiplication.

left_bound.description: An optional timeline/index limit anchoring the start of a CDQ recursion branch.

left_index.description: The starting point used to frame an operation recursively on the left side of a dataset.

left_or_target_index.description: The single coordinate updated, or the start of a range queried in a persistent tree.

left_partition_vertices.description: The subset of vertices explicitly defined as the 'left' side of a bipartite matching problem.

left_to_right_first.description: Dictates the initial sweep direction (true = L->R, false = R->L) for a zigzag traversal.

left_treap_root.description: The root of the treap containing strictly smaller implicit or explicit keys prior to a merge.

left_version_root.description: An optional root pointer representing an older tree state to subtract from the current query.

line_1.description: The geometric coefficients or coordinates defining the first line in space.

line_2.description: The geometric coefficients or coordinates defining the second line in space.

line_segments_list.description: The entire collection of individual geometric segments to be checked for overlap.

list_a.description: The entry node for the first ordered Linked List sequence.

list_b.description: The entry node for the second ordered Linked List sequence.

load_factor.description: The current ratio of elements to buckets dictating when a map structure resizes.

load_factor_threshold.description: The predefined decimal limit (e.g., 0.75) that triggers dynamic resizing of hash structures.

lookup_table.description: A precomputed array of size 32 or 64 mapping De Bruijn hash values to trailing zero counts.

low_bound.description: The explicit lower search limit indicating the minimum possible valid answer.

low_bound_l.description: The starting point defining the base of an offset segmented mathematical sieve.

low_index.description: The lowest valid index framing the bottom of a search or partition space.

low_key.description: The inclusive lower limit value filtering a range search across a BST structure.

low_value.description: The smallest pivot category used to group elements in Dutch National Flag sorting.

lower_bound.description: The current constraint indicating that no node constructed below this point can have a smaller value.

lower_bound_number.description: The start of the numerical range over which digit DP properties are counted.

main_tree_root.description: The entry point of the larger topology being searched for a structural match.

make_circular.description: A flag to bind the final tail pointer of a flattened BST back to the head.

max_allowed_height_diff.description: The tolerance limit (usually 1) for the difference between left and right subtrees in AVL validation.

max_bit_width.description: The fixed depth of a bitwise Trie representing the largest possible binary string length.

max_bound.description: The dynamic constraint representing the largest allowable value for nodes in the current BST subtree.

max_colors_m.description: The strict upper limit on the number of distinct labels permitted to color a graph.

max_combinations_count.description: An early termination bound that aborts backtracking once enough valid sets are generated.

max_consecutive_same_color.description: The constraint limiting how many adjacent objects can share an identical label (usually 2 in Paint Fence).

max_deadline_limit.description: An optional bound representing the absolute latest time slot available across all scheduled tasks.

max_depth_limit.description: The strict search depth at which Iterative Deepening DFS is forced to truncate and backtrack.

max_digits.description: The total number of sorting passes Radix Sort must perform, derived from the longest string/number.

max_edge_weight_w.description: The largest individual link cost in a graph, defining the width of Dial's bucket queue array.

max_eviction_steps.description: The cycle threshold determining when a Cuckoo hash table gives up and triggers a rehash.

max_flow_subroutine.description: The internal max-flow algorithm (e.g., Dinic's) called N-1 times to build a Gomory-Hu Tree.

max_jump_lengths.description: An array where each element specifies the farthest reach allowed from that current index.

max_jump_steps.description: The maximum forward distance permissible per action (e.g., 2 in standard Climbing Stairs).

max_level_limit.description: The absolute maximum height a Skip List's express lanes are permitted to reach.

max_log_height.description: The computed size of the secondary dimension in a binary lifting table (ceil(log2(N))).

max_segment_value.description: The numerical ceiling (usually 255) for any single partitioned block in IP address generation.

max_state_size.description: An array preallocation limit governing the memory footprint of bitset-based DP.

max_suggestions_limit.description: A cap limiting the total volume of words retrieved during an autocomplete Trie search.

max_target_sum.description: The total bitset capacity constraining the bounds of a subset sum shift-or approach.

max_transactions.description: An optional generic constraint limiting the total buy/sell cycles permitted over the timeline.

max_transactions_k.description: The explicit multi-dimensional state bound limiting total trades in Stock Buy-Sell IV.

max_valid_code.description: The upper bound (e.g., 26 for alphabets) for grouping adjacent numeric characters in Decode Ways.

max_value.description: The absolute maximum numeric value establishing the frequency array size for Counting Sort.

maximize_flag.description: If true, the Simplex algorithm flips its objective logic to maximize rather than minimize.

maximize_instead_of_minimize.description: Inverts the Hungarian algorithm's cost matrix to find maximum weight matching instead of minimum.

maze_grid.description: The 2D representation of open paths and walls navigated by a backtracking solver.

merge_cost_function.description: A formula returning the specific penalty or weight added when combining two adjacent intervals in DP.

merge_subtrees_fn.description: A delegate that dictates how the independent properties of multiple child branches are combined.

mid_value.description: The central pivot element bounding the 'equals' partition in 3-way Dutch National Flag sorting.

min_alphabet_value.description: The smallest discrete symbol in the sequence, establishing the bottom bound for Wavelet Tree splits.

min_bound.description: The dynamic constraint representing the smallest allowable value for nodes in the current BST subtree.

min_candy_per_child.description: The baseline minimum resource guaranteed to every entity regardless of rating.

min_survivable_health.description: The floor value (usually 1) that health cannot drop below during Dungeon Game reverse DP.

min_value.description: The absolute minimum numeric value used as an offset for the Counting Sort frequency array.

moduli_array.description: The set of pairwise coprime integers defining the moduli bases for the Chinese Remainder Theorem.

modulus.description: An optional global wrapper that applies modulo arithmetic to all intermediate DP/math operations.

modulus_is_prime_flag.description: If true, enables Fermat's Little Theorem as a shortcut for inverse generation; if false, forces Extended GCD.

modulus_m.description: The exact integer constraint wrapping computations for modular arithmetic loops.

modulus_p.description: The prime group order utilized during discrete logarithm phase steps.

monotonic_direction.description: A parameter indicating if a queue/stack maintains an 'increasing' or 'decreasing' sequence.

most_significant_digit_first.description: If true, list heads represent the largest place value; if false, lists are processed in reverse.

multiplicand_a.description: The value being multiplied repeatedly via shifts in a bitwise multiplication algorithm.
